TPHCM và Nam Bộ kết thúc mùa mưa trong nửa đầu tháng 11
(Dân trí) - Mưa tại Nam Bộ được dự báo tập trung trong 10 ngày đầu tháng 11, sau đó giảm dần. Đáng chú ý, lượng mưa tại TPHCM có thể thấp hơn trung bình nhiều năm 10-30%.
Đài Khí tượng Thủy văn Nam Bộ dự báo, ngày 2/11, TPHCM và các tỉnh, thành Nam Bộ có mưa rào và dông vài nơi, riêng chiều và tối có mưa rào, dông rải rác.
Nhiệt độ thấp nhất trong ngày dao động 23-26 độ C, cao nhất 31-34 độ C. Người dân cần đề phòng các cơn dông có thể đi kèm lốc, sét và gió giật mạnh.
Theo cơ quan khí tượng, trong tháng 11, hiện tượng El Nino tiếp tục hoạt động với cường độ rất mạnh. Không khí lạnh từ lục địa Trung Quốc liên tục tăng cường xuống nước ta nhưng chỉ tác động yếu đến khu vực Nam Bộ.
Mùa mưa ở TPHCM và Nam Bộ dự báo kết thúc trong nửa đầu tháng 11 (Ảnh: Hoàng Hướng).
Trong khoảng 10 ngày đầu tháng 11, rãnh thấp xích đạo kết hợp với hội tụ gió trên cao có thể gây mưa tại Nam Bộ. Tuy nhiên, từ giữa đến cuối tháng, áp cao cận nhiệt đới hạ trục xuống phía nam và chi phốithời tiếtkhu vực, khiến mưa giảm dần. Mùa mưa tại Nam Bộ được dự báo kết thúc trong nửa đầu tháng 11.
Nền nhiệt trung bình tháng 11 tại Nam Bộ phổ biến cao hơn trung bình nhiều năm 0,3-1 độ C. Nhiệt độ cao nhất phổ biến 30-33 độ C, có ngày tăng lên 34-36 độ C; nhiệt độ thấp nhất phổ biến 24-27 độ C, riêng khu vực phía Bắc có nơi dưới 24 độ C.
Lượng mưa trong tháng 11 được dự báo xấp xỉ đến thấp hơn trung bình nhiều năm. Đáng chú ý, khu vực trung tâm TPHCM có thể thiếu hụt lượng mưa từ 10% đến 30% so với mức trung bình nhiều năm.
Mưa tập trung chủ yếu trong khoảng 10 ngày đầu tháng, sau đó giảm dần. Tổng số ngày mưa trong tháng phổ biến 8-13 ngày.
Trên vùng biển Nam Bộ, gió mùa Đông Bắc hoạt động với cường độ trung bình đến mạnh. Cơ quan khí tượng nhận định ít có khả năng xuất hiện xoáy thuận nhiệt đới trên Biển Đông trong tháng này.
Cơ quan khí tượng khuyến cáo, người dân đề phòng các cơn dông kèm lốc, sét và gió giật mạnh, có thể gây nguy hiểm cho người và thiệt hại tài sản. Trên biển, các đợt gió mùa Đông Bắc mạnh kết hợp thời tiết xấu có thể ảnh hưởng đến hoạt động của tàu thuyền.
TPHCM và Nam Bộ ngày nắng, chiều tối đề phòng mưa dông
TPHCM và Nam Bộ ngày có nắng, chiều và tối nhiều khu vực xuất hiện mưa rào và dông. Người dân cần đề phòng lốc, sét và gió giật mạnh.
TPHCM và Nam Bộ giảm mưa, nắng nóng cuối tuần
Mưa tại TPHCM và Nam Bộ có xu hướng giảm dần đến hết cuối tuần, trong khi nắng xuất hiện nhiều hơn. Tuy nhiên, chiều tối, một số khu vực vẫn có mưa rào và dông rải rác.
TPHCM và Nam Bộ tiếp tục xuất hiện triều cường
TPHCM và Nam Bộ có mưa rào và dông rải rác vào chiều tối, có nơi mưa to. Những ngày tới, triều cường tiếp tục dâng, làm tăng nguy cơ ngập tại các khu vực ven sông, kênh rạch và vùng trũng thấp.
TPHCM và Nam Bộ có mưa dông diện rộng vào cuối tuần
TPHCM và Nam Bộ được dự báo tiếp tục có mưa dông diện rộng trong 3 ngày 16-18/10. Người dân cần đề phòng lốc, sét, gió giật mạnh và ngập úng khi mưa lớn.

Bệnh viện ứng phó xuất toán bảo hiểm y tế
Duy Tính- nguyenduytinhbtn@gmail.com30/10/2026 13:21 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!Xuất toán bảo hiểm y tế là nỗi 'ám ảnh' của nhân viên y tế và bệnh viện, vì vậy cần phải kiểm soát được chỉ định, làm tốt hồ sơ bệnh án, quy trình thanh toán.
Tại Hội nghị khoa học kỹ thuật Bệnh viện Trưng Vương năm 2026 diễn ra ngày 30.10, thạc sĩ, bác sĩ chuyên khoa II Phan Thanh Hằng, Trưởng phòng Kế hoạch tổng hợp của bệnh viện này đã chia sẻ thực trạng xuất toán bảo hiểm y tế tại đơn vị trong năm 2024 - 2025 và các giải pháp khắc phục.
Số liệu tại Bệnh viện Trưng Vương cho thấy số lượt điều trị năm 2025 tăng khoảng 4,8% so với năm 2024, nhưng chi phí đề nghịbảo hiểm y tếthanh toán tăng 10%.
Tỷ lệ từ chối thanh toán giảm từ 0,43% vào năm 2024 xuống 0,29% vào năm 2025. Tổng số tiền xuất toán năm 2025 giảm 25% so với năm trước. Tuy nhiên, các lỗi liên quan đến thuốc, dịch vụ kỹ thuật và cận lâm sàng vẫn lặp lại qua nhiều quý.
Bệnh nhân đi khám chữa bệnh bảo hiểm y tế tại Bệnh viện Trưng Vương
Đáng chú ý, chi phí điều trị nội trú tăng 16,4%. Bình quân một ca điều trị năm 2025 gần 12 triệu đồng, so với khoảng 10 triệu đồng năm 2024. Các khoản tăng chủ yếu là ngày giường, vật tư y tế và thuốc.
Trong đó, chi phí ngày giường tăng một phần do giá mới theo nghị quyết quy định giá cụ thể dịch vụ khám chữa bệnh tại các cơ sở y tế nhà nước thuộc TP.HCM quản lý và tình trạng kéo dài ngày điều trị. Tỷ lệ ngày điều trị kéo dài tại bệnh viện là 8,3%, hơn mức của các cơ sở trên toàn quốc và thành phố.
Nhiều nhóm chi phí được bảo hiểm y tế giám sát
Theo bác sĩ Phan Thanh Hằng, trong 8 tháng đầu năm 2026, quỹ bảo hiểm y tế tại TP.HCM đã sử dụng gần 80% số tiền dự kiến chi cả năm, tương đương gần 24.000 tỉ đồng; nguy cơ vượt dự toán hơn 4.500 tỉ đồng.
Trong khi số lượt khám chữa bệnh chỉ tăng khoảng 7,1% nhưng chi phí liên quan vật tư y tế, xét nghiệm tăng cao hơn 2 - 3 lần. Bên cạnh đó, chi phí chẩn đoán hình ảnh, tiền giường và tiền thuốc cũng tăng. Đây là những nội dung được bảo hiểm y tế tập trung giám sát trong các tháng cuối năm 2026.
Bảo hiểm xã hội TP.HCM sẽ giám sát 6 lỗi thường gặp nhất. Trong đó, tập trung vào những cơ sở thuộc luồng đỏ có chi phí tăng bất thường, tỷ lệ nhập viện cao, xét nghiệm hoặc chẩn đoán hình ảnh tăng đột biến. Cơ quan này cũng lọc trùng thuốc, xét nghiệm; kiểm soát chỉ định chụp CT-Scanner, MRI lặp lại trong thời gian ngắn nhưng không phù hợp.
Ngoài ra, các nội dung được kiểm soát gồm chi phí điều trị nội trú, đối soát hồ sơ bệnh án, giá thuốc và vật tư y tế, nhất là tại những cơ sở có chi phí cao hơn 5% so với nơi khác.
Các bệnh viện cần tuân thủ quy trình khám chữa bệnh và thanh quyết toán bảo hiểm y tế tránh bị xuất toán
Kiềm soát từ chỉ định đến hồ sơ bệnh án
Để hạn chế xuất toán bảo hiểm y tế, theo bác sĩ Phan Thanh Hằng, cơ sở y tế cần nắm căn cứ pháp lý đối với từng nhóm chi phí.
Chỉ định lâm sàng chỉ được thanh toán khi dịch vụ thực tế được thực hiện, đúng cơ sở, chuyên môn, phạm vi hành nghề, đúng bệnh, đúng đối tượng và đủ điều kiện thanh toán. Dữ liệu phải được mã hóa XML chính xác trước khi gửi lên cổng đề nghị thanh toán bảo hiểm y tế.
Năm 2025, thống kê trên toàn quốc, lỗi liên quan đến thanh toánbảo hiểm y tếnhiều nhất là dịch vụ kỹ thuật, vật tư y tế, thuốc, mã hóa, áp giá và danh mục.
Vì vậy, bác sĩ cần chú ý chẩn đoán, bệnh cận lâm sàng và đặc biệt liên quan đến giá, cân nhắc lựa chọn thuốc cùng hoạt chất có giá phổ biến hơn. Xem xét kết quả xét nghiệm đã có trước khi chỉ định lặp lại như HbA1c, mỡ máu hoặc xét nghiệm tầm soát. Với vật tư, thiết bị y tế, chú ý lỗi thường liên quan đến kiểm định, vượt công suất, quy trình đấu thầu và áp mã thiết bị. Ngoài ra, còn có sai sót về nhân sự, chấm công phạm vi hành nghề, ngày giường, định mức và thời gian điều trị cũng cần phải quan tâm.
"Hồ sơ bệnh án phải ghi đầy đủ diễn biến, căn cứ chỉ định, chữ ký của bác sĩ, điều dưỡng, người bệnh và giờ thực hiện; tránh sao chép nội dung giữa các ngày hoặc hồ sơ bệnh nhân", bác sĩ Hằng nói.
Ngoài vai trò kiểm soát của các khoa phòng, theo bác sĩ Phan Thanh Hằng,Bệnh viện Trưng Vươngđã ứng dụng phần mềm tự động hóa xử lý, phân tích dữ liệu phục vụ giám định bảo hiểm y tế. Công cụ có 11 chức năng, cho phép gộp nhiều tệp Excel, rút ngắn thời gian xử lý dữ liệu.
Thời gian tới, bệnh viện tiếp tục rà soát ngày điều trị, tiền giám định nội bộ, ứng dụng công nghệ thông tin cảnh báo, kiểm soát giá thuốc, vật tư, danh mục kỹ thuật và nhân sự; đồng thời tăng cường đào tạo, phối hợp giữa các khoa, phòng.
Bác sĩ Hằng nhấn mạnh mỗi y lệnh là một quyết định thanh toán, hồ sơ bệnh án là bằng chứng quan trọng để giải trình với cơ quan bảo hiểm xã hội. Vì vậy, chỉ định phải có căn cứ, dữ liệu và hồ sơ phải đầy đủ, chính xác để kiểm soát chi phí, hạn chế xuất toán.
Bác sĩ chuyên khoa II Huỳnh Ngọc Hớn, Giám đốc Bệnh viện Trưng Vương, cho biết Hội nghị khoa học kỹ thuật năm 2026 của bệnh viện tổ chức với 2 chuyên đề chính nội khoa và ngoại khoa. Các báo cáo tập trung vào nghiên cứu thực tiễn của bệnh viện, trong đó có những tiến bộ về bỏng, tạo hình thẩm mỹ, chăm sóc vết thương, ngoại tổng quát, điều trị cột sống, tim mạch, hô hấp, tiêu hóa, điều dưỡng.
Bệnh viện cũng mời báo cáo viên từ bệnh viện khác chia sẻ kinh nghiệm.
Bệnh viện Trưng Vương là bệnh viện đa khoa hạng 1 trực thuộc Sở Y tế TP.HCM. Bên cạnh phục vụ bệnh nhân tại bệnh viện, phát triển các chuyên khoa sâu, nghiên cứu khoa học, bệnh viện xác định chương trình khám sức khỏe toàn dân là nhiệm vụ chính trị quan trọng. WSL talking points: Kang could have a problem and how long can Slegers hang on?
Arsenal dropped points again despite dominating while Lauren James had to go off in Chelsea’s 6-0 win at Charlton
Lionesses may present Uefa with problem
London City Lionesses may have lost 2-1 to champions Manchester City, but their performance and league position have shown their European aspirations are far from unrealistic. Aided by Arsenal’s poor start, London City are third in the WSL table and were frustrated to end the day with a six-point gap to the top two after dominating in Bromley. “It’s doubly frustrating, because I think the result was not the one we deserve,” said their coach, Eder Maestre. “Manchester City are more mature. They are more used to it. When you have this consistency and you are very used to playing these kinds of games, maybe you have more experience.” Maestre’s team have a three-point lead over fourth-placed Tottenham and if they continue their upwards trajectory and qualify for the Champions League, Uefa will be forced to tackle the possible scenario of two Michelle Kang-owned clubs, London City and OL Lyonnes, qualifying sooner than they perhaps anticipated.Suzanne Wrack
Match report: London City Lionesses 1-2 Manchester City
It was groundhog day for Arsenal against Aston Villa with the Gunners going a goal down for the fifth time this season. “We just said it feels like we’re playing the same game over and over again,” said the manager, Renée Slegers. “We go one goal down from a break and we don’t start with enough urgency.” The issue for Arsenal is that opposition teams can sense this lack of urgency. Get one chance early on, take it and then capitalise on the fact that Slegers’ side just cannot break down a low block. How Slegers, her staff and the squad arrest this malaise that is preventing any intensity or clinical play is the big unanswered question. Thewins against Tottenhamand Benficafelt like the seeds of a turnaround in fortunes, but they papered over cracks that will be exposed again until they make more of their dominance in the final third.SW

Chart showing how many times clubs have conceded the first goal of the game in the 2026-27 Women’s Super LeagueView image in fullscreenArsenal’s struggles continue at both ends of the pitch.Photograph: Jody Demay-Davies/SPP/Shutterstock
James injury ruins Chelsea’s perfect day
There is significant concern over Lauren James’ fitness after she suffered another injury blow against Charlton. The 25-year-old was forced off the pitch after pulling up off the ball in the 35th minute. “It is difficult to say,” Sonia Bompastor updated. “I can only say it’s her hamstring and we’ll assess her later to have more detailed information.” It is the latest fitness worry for the England international who, after being limited to just 11 and six league starts in the last two campaigns respectively, had started this season in superb form with four goals in the WSL. It was the only blemish on an otherwise enjoyable afternoon for the league leaders who ran out 6-0 winners at The Valley. Defender Nathalie Björn marked her first start after months on the sidelines with the opener. Substitute Aggie Beever-Jones ended her barren spell, scoring her first league goal since September 2025. There was also an emotional moment for young Italian midfielder Giulia Dragoni who opened her Chelsea account after coming off the bench.Sophie Downey
WSL roundup: James injured in Chelsea’s win over Charlton
Spence makes history in Spurs victory
As she led Tottenham Hotspur out at St Andrew’s, Drew Spence wrote herself into the history books. Her start against Birmingham City marked her 217th in the WSL, making her the competition’s new all-time record appearance holder. It was the latest accolade of a decorated career that has seen her win five league titles, four FA Cups and two League Cups. The 34-year-old Jamaica international featured in the inaugural WSL season back in 2011 with Chelsea where she spent 14 years before switching to Spurs in 2022. She was once again at the heart of Martin Ho’s midfield as Tottenham ended their three-game losing streak with a dominant 4-1 win over the Blues. Spurs were back to their attacking best, registering 11 of their 29 chances on target and recording 61 touches in the opposition box and having four different goalscorers. It was a victory that moved them up to fourth in the table.SD
Asseyi shines in Liverpool thrashing
Viviane Asseyi put on a performance Zinedine Zidane would be proud of as West Ham stormed to a dominant 4-1 victory against Liverpool. The 32-year-old scored twice for the Hammers on Sunday, the second goal a brilliant free-kick from the edge of the box which flew into the top-right corner. Asseyi told the Guardian recently thatshe grew up wanting to be likethe former France international – and that excellent strike was Zidane-esque. Her double in east London took the forward up to five goals for the season, moving her to joint fifth in the Golden Boot race. “She missed a hat-trick unfortunately but I’m very happy,” the West Ham head coach, Rita Guarino, said. “She’s an incredible player. Very happy for her, very happy in the way the team help her to make this kind of performance.”Emillia Hawkins

Everton and United need flair in window
Is creativity a problem for both of these sides? On Saturday’s evidence, yes. There was a Welsh derby in each of the first five rounds of the 2026-27 URC season
Cardiff, Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets are ready for November breaks after completing the first block of the domestic 2026-27 season.
The United Rugby Championship (URC) is on hold while four rounds are played in the Nations Championship.
Cardiff and Dragons are setting the pace on 14 points, with the seventh-placed Blue and Blacks edging in front on win count.
Ospreys and Scarlets have work to do but have got their tough double-headers in South Africa out of the way.
There has also been a round of European rugby, with the Blue and Blacks losing in the Champions Cup and the other three winning in the second-tier Challenge Cup.
How will the Welsh quartet reflect on a first chunk of the season that featured a derby in every league round?
Centre Hawkins determined to make World Cup
The Prem talents hunting Wales breakthroughs
Wales wing Josh Adams has scored on both his Cardiff starts in 2026-27
Cardiff were Wales' standard bearers in 2025-26 when they finished sixth and qualified for the play-offs for the first time.
The Blue and Blacks have been a mixed bag, but got acrucial 26-0 win against Ospreysin Swansea to finish.
"We have been fighting for a performance like that all of this first block," said lock Josh McNally.
"The group is in a really good place and everybody is aligned with what we want to do. When it clicks we can put in a performance like that."
It was a strong response to a rare poor display at the Arms Park against Sharks, which had the mitigation of a five-day turnaround from a defeat by English champions Northampton.
Taine Bashamhas been a stand-out performer at number eight to earn a Wales recall, while hugely promising 20-year-old centre Steffan Emanuel capped a strong first block with a man-of-the-match performance at Ospreys.
"The break is at a decent time which will allow us to work on stuff we haven't been so great at, then go again for a massive run of games," said head coach Corniel van Zyl.
Cardiff will mix their URC play-off bid with facing top-tier European opposition in the next block.
They have a mouth-watering home Champions Cup fixture against Bath in December, then games against Stade Francais and Montpellier.
Northampton28-12 Cardiff (Champions Cup)
Harrison Keddie made his 150th Dragons appearance against Zebre
Dragons head coach Filo Tiatia declared that he was content with their first block after his side avoided a slipagainst winless Zebre.
"I am happy with where we are, but we have a lot of work to do," he said.
"The next block is so important and it's five weeks before we hit Edinburgh, then there are nine games to Munster at the end of January.
"We need everyone fit, fresh and ready to scrap for the club."
The November break is timely for Dragons, whose squad was creaking for Zebre.
They were without 18 players due to five Wales calls and injuries, while several players were bruised and battered.
That comes after an encouraging first block that featured three wins, a draw and a missed opportunity at Benetton but two disappointments against Ospreys.
Dragons got their Challenge Cup campaign off to a winning start against Perpignan and have 14 points in the URC.
That is half of last year's total, although they are yet to play a side that made the 2026 play-offs and none of those they have faced are in the current top half.
The driving line-out has been a weapon, Tonga wing Anzelo Tuitavuki has scored tries in five successive games and the attack looks more threatening.
"We got some stats through at the end of last season around where we sat in terms of our attacking game," said coach Matt O'Brien.
"We were pretty good at our launch stuff - our line-out and scrum attack - but our unstructured game needed a bit of work.
"We focused heavily on that and have had some good improvements, with our offloading one of those areas."
Dragons will hope theirWales contingentof Aneurin Owen, Che Hope, Dillon Lewis, Ben Carter and Seb Davies, Argentina prop Rodrigo Martinez and Tongans Tuitavuki, Fetuli Paea and Fine Inisi come back unscathed.

Former Australia captain Liam Wright qualifies for Wales in 2027
It looked set to be an encouraging first block for Ospreys until they were thumped by Cardiff and Mark Jones’ side will spend the next month reflecting ruefully on such a humbling home defeat in a local derby.
Ospreys racked up the air miles while major work was done to get St Helen's ready for their Swansea homecoming.
Jones has given 35 players starts, rotating due to a schedule that saw them play in Durban, Johannesburg, Newport and Tbilisi.
Former Australia captain Liam Wright has been a positive as he attempts to put several years of injury misfortune behind him.
The blind-side flanker has started all five URC games and impressed with his work rate, line-out skills and leadership.
A rib injury suffered on debut means that former Wallabies wing Marika Koroibete has not been able to make the same impact in the first block.
A double of Dragons, with a maximum 10 points, ensures that is remains a solid start, despite being nilled by Cardiff.
Jones said: "We are still a big work in progress. There is lots to do in our game, including the consistency with which we do things.
"It was a nice little reminder of the level that you need to get to in the URC if you want to get victories."
Three of Ospreys' next four fixtures are at St Helen's - with champions Leinster next up on Friday, 4 December.
"We've got to ponder on the Cardiff defeat and get the work in, because you can't expect results for work you don't do," said Jones.

Nigel Davies' side made another slow start to the campaign with derby defeats against Cardiff and Scarlets.

How you brush your teeth — and what you use to do it — matters.

Recently, dentistDr. Jin-Ho Pharksays he's noticed patients asking about fluoride-free toothpaste options. Phark is an associate professor of clinical dentistry at the Herman Ostrow School of Dentistry of University of Southern California.
"There's a lot of interest from the patients," Phark says. "I hear that also regularly from students."
One product that patients are asking about in particular is a calcium phosphate mineral called hydroxyapatite. Many patients, Phark says, may have seen the products on social media, "being pushed by influencers and other people quite intensively."
The traditional fluoride toothpaste became common in thelate 1950s, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, when Procter & Gamble Co. released Crest nationally. Over the next few decades, oral care products with fluoride as their active ingredient became widely available around the world. These products help protect the outer layer of teeth from cavity-causing bacteria.
And dental health is important because it's related to so many systems in your body, from yourheartto digestion.
Want the latest stories on the science of healthy living? Subscribe to NPR'sHealth newsletter.
"There are these connections made between your oral health, and the bugs that you have in your mouth, and systemic health and even the composition of your gut microbiome," saysDr. Livia Tenuta, a dentist who specializes in preventing tooth decay and associate professor at the University of Michigan School of Dentistry.
The promise of hydroxyapatite? Many of the things you care about when it comes to toothpaste: cavity protection, whitening, enamel-strengthening. But without fluoride.
Health experts widely agree that fluoride — a naturally occurring mineral — is beneficial to health. But curiosity is growing about fluoride-free options.
"There is an increasing number of people who are refusing fluoride totally, or hesitant to take it, especially for their children," saysBennett Amaechi, a professor of dentistry at the University of Texas at San Antonio.
That hesitancy stems from a history of skepticism about fluoride. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. hasblamed the fluoridation of waterfor a number of health problems, including arthritis, bone fractures, bone cancer, IQ loss, neurodevelopmental disorders and thyroid disease.
Low levels of fluoride are generally considered safe and key to preventing cavities. Amaechi says there's no concrete evidence about potential harms of fluoride when it comes to children's IQ. Andresearchthat has found associations between fluoride and IQ has looked at very high levels of fluoride — over twice what'srecommendedin the U.S. water supply. The CDC previously named the addition of fluoride to public drinking water one of thetop 10 great public health achievements of the 20th century, alongside vaccinations and family planning. They also say fluoride in waterreduces cavities by 25%.
Still, Kennedy's criticism of fluoride seems to have made its way to toothpaste — and opened up space for products that use hydroxyapatite instead.
The hype around hydroxyapatite is, in part, due to its similarity to tooth enamel. There's also some research that suggests hydroxyapatitecan helpwith tooth sensitivity.
Fluoride analysis triggers renewed debate over what levels are safe for kids
Tooth enamel is mostly made of calcium and phosphate. Those minerals form the outer layer of your teeth, which protects the internal layers of tissues, nerves and blood vessels, from damage.
Your enamel is stronger than your bones, but still susceptible to damage over time from things like sugary foods and dental plaque. Bacteria in your mouth feed on sugars, and produce acids that eat away at the outer layer of your teeth. Tenuta says over time, that process sets the stage for tooth decay, often referred to ascaries, or eventually cavities (a hole in a tooth that comes from this decay).
She says fluoride toothpaste helps protect teeth by "remineralizing" them with calcium and phosphate.
"When [fluoride is] available in our saliva, in the dental plaque that we were not very perfect in brushing, that fluoride that is left over after brushing with the fluoride toothpaste will actually bring minerals back to the tooth," Tenuta says.
Fluoride works with those minerals to form a new compound that protects teeth. It acts like a shield for your enamel. But you need to brush with fluoride toothpaste consistently. Dentists recommend twice daily to keep those minerals around in our mouths.
Hydroxyapatite is thought to work in a slightly different way. These products seem to get into tiny crevicesin the tooth enamel.
Many hydroxyapatite products use a form called nano-hydroxyapatite, which has smaller particles that, in theory, can more easily penetrate pores in enamel, though research data is limited.
Amaechi, who studies hydroxyapatite use, says fluoride is extensively researched, especially in long-term studies. But he says early research on hydroxyapatite is positive.

Mbappe và Bellingham tỏa sáng, Real Madrid bám đuổi Barcelona, Atletico
(Dân trí) - Real Madrid thể hiện phong độ ổn định khi giành chiến thắng 3-0 trên sân của Racing Santander ở vòng 11 La Liga sáng 2/11 nhờ sự tỏa sáng của Mbappe và Bellingham.
Hành quân đến sân của Racing, Real Madrid sử dụng đội hình thiên về tấn công với bộ ba tiền đạo Jude Bellingham, Yan Diomande và Kylian Mbappe. Real Madrid đẩy cao đội hình lên tấn công và nhanh chóng tạo ra sức ép lớn lên phần sân đối phương.
Mbappe tỏa sáng trong chiến thắng của Real Madrid (Ảnh: Getty).
Ngay phút thứ 10, KylianMbappebị Matteo Prati phạm lỗi trong vòng cấm, đội khách được hưởng phạt đền. Trên chấm 11m ở phút 11, tiền đạo người Pháp bình tĩnh đánh bại thủ môn Julen Agirrezabala, mở tỷ số trận đấu 1-0 cho đoàn quân HLV Mourinho.
Racing Santander thể hiện quyết tâm tìm kiếm bàn gỡ hòa. Phút 13, Iker Luque tung cú dứt điểm trong vòng cấm nhưng thủ môn Thibaut Courtois kịp thời dùng chân cản phá, cứu thua cho Real Madrid.
Thầy trò HLV Mourinho thể hiện bản lĩnh khi bị ép sân, phút 21, Mbappe phối hợp với Arda Guler trước khi tiền vệ người Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ thực hiện đường chuyền thuận lợi cho Jude Bellingham. Tiền vệ người Anh thoát xuống, dứt điểm chính xác, nâng tỷ số lên 2-0 cho đội khách.
Đến phút 36, từ quả phạt góc do Guler thực hiện, hàng thủ Racing Santander phá bóng không tốt. Yan Diomande tung cú vô lê từ ngoài vòng cấm, đưa bóng găm thẳng vào góc cao khung thành trong sự bất lực của Agirrezabala. Real Madrid khép lại hiệp 1 với chiến thắng 3-0.
Jude Bellingham lập công giúp Real Madrid thắng Racing 3-0 (Ảnh: Getty).
Sau hiệp 2, Racing Santander nỗ lực đẩy cao đội hình nhưng các pha dứt điểm của đội chủ nhà thiếu chính xác hoặc không thể vượt qua hàng phòng ngự Real Madrid. Phút 53, Yassir Zabiri tung cú sút trong vòng cấm lại đưa bóng đi vọt xà ngang.
Mbappe cũng có nhiểu cơ hội, nhưng ngôi sao người Pháp lại dứt điểm quá vội vàng. Real Madrid chủ động chơi phòng ngự để bảo toàn lợi thế. Về cuối trận, trọng tài cho Racing Santander hưởng phạt đền vì tình huống bóng chạm tay Aurelien Tchouameni, nhưng ông thay đổi quyết định sau khi tham khảo công nghệ VAR.
Real Madrid tưởng như có bàn thắng thứ 4 khi Bellingham đưa bóng vào lưới Racing, nhưng bàn thắng không được công nhận vì lỗi việt vị. Chiến thắng 3-0 trước Racing giúp Real Madrid tiếp tục đứng thứ ba trên bảng xếp hạng La Liga với 27 điểm, kém Atletico Madrid 1 điểm và kém Barcelona 3 điểm.

evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq1k:
Supermarket freezers in Belgium and Sweden hit by suspected cyber-attack - BBC News
Image source,AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption,
Freezers have had to be emptied at several ICA grocery stores in Sweden after the cyber-attack
Dozens of supermarkets in Belgium and Sweden have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting its refrigerators and freezers.
Around 40 Delhaize supermarkets and 15 Carrefour stores were affected in Belgium, while several ICA and Coop shops in Sweden were hit. Thirteen SuperValu shops have also been impacted in Ireland.
Thousands of euros worth of food has had to be thrown away, according to local media reports, with one ICA store in Sweden saying temperatures for its freezers had been set to 50 C (122F).
It is not clear who is behind the attack, which follows a similar incident last monththat affected hundreds of French supermarkets.
Delhaize, one of Belgium's biggest supermarket chains, told Belgian media a "computer incident" had occurred overnight at 40 shops.
Carrefour, a French-owned supermarket, said it was "currently analysing" the incident at 15 of its Belgian stores.
Meanwhile, a spokesperson for ICA in Sweden confirmed the incident had affected a "small number of ICA stores operating outside ICA's central network".
"ICA is currently supporting the affected stores in managing the situation," they said.
One of the IVA branches located in Sjöbo, southern Sweden, wrote on social media: "Our refrigerators and freezers have been hacked overnight and they have set the temperature to 50 degrees."
The store was closed earlier but has now reopened to customers.
Seven out of the 800 Coop stores in Sweden are also affected but the "situation is currently contained and under control", the company told the BBC.

An ICA employee in Stockholm cleans out a fridge after supermarket cooling systems across Europe were hit by temperature problems overnight.Photograph: Fredrik Sandberg/TT News Agency/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAn ICA employee in Stockholm cleans out a fridge after supermarket cooling systems across Europe were hit by temperature problems overnight.Photograph: Fredrik Sandberg/TT News Agency/AFP/Getty Images
Supermarket freezers across Europe hit by second suspected cyber-attack
Chains in Sweden, Belgium and Luxembourg say fridge temperatures rose overnight, similar to hack of French stores
Supermarket chains in Sweden, Belgium andLuxembourghave said the temperatures of their refrigerators and freezers in dozens of stores rose overnight, prompting fears of a cyber-attack similar to one that caused millions of euros of food losses in France.
Sweden’s Coop chain toldthe daily Aftonbladeton Monday that six of ​its stores ‌had been ​affected, while ICA said it was “aware that a limited ​number of stores were affected by an incident overnight which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems”.
The Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize, which last ​month ​reported a ​cybersecurity ‌incident ​to police in the Netherlands, said an “IT incident” ​had hit fridges and ⁠freezers in dozens of its ⁠supermarkets in ​Belgium ‌and ‌Luxembourg.
A company spokesperson, Sarah ‌De Meester, said the supermarket chain had established that temperatures in the cooling systems had increased, adding that the incident was being investigated.
Belgium’sLe Soir newspaper reportedthat dozens of stores and supermarkets were affected, including five Spar outlets, multiple Shop & Go convenience stores attached to Q8 service stations, and a number of smaller Proxy Delhaize minimarkets.
“We started mobilising technicians at 1am,” Stephan Moelans, the chief executive of Sabcobel, which specialises in refrigeration system installations, told the paper. “We spent all night and morning disconnecting the affected installations from the grid.”
Not cool: who hacked France’s supermarket fridges?Read more
French ⁠police said in October thathackers had seized control of cooling units at ⁠up to 700 supermarketsin a large-scale attack that led to heavy losses of chilled and frozen foods and underlined the vulnerability of internet-connected systems.
Hackers had remotely overridden the settings on thousands of freezers, fridges and chiller cabinets, pushing them from as low as -27C to well over 50C. The Intermarché, Coopérative U, Carrefour, Leclerc and Monoprix chains were among those affected.
Stores had to discard vast quantities of fresh meat, dairy and frozen products, with many suffering losses ranging from tens of thousands of euros to more than €130,000 (£109,000). Two stores in Alsace reported a combined loss of €270,000.
Most supermarket cold aisles are connected to the internet to allow remote maintenance and alerts for system failures. In the French attack, the hackers pirated controllers mostly supplied by the Danish company Danfoss.
They disabled alarm systems before adjusting the thermostats or extending the defrost programme by hours. Danfoss said it had identified security flaws last year and had “long recommended” customers install updates.
The Paris prosecutor’s office has opened a formal investigatiion into the French attack, saying damage included “food losses and fires”, and the prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, instructed France’s national cybersecurity agency, ANSSI, to investigate.
ANSSI subsequently confirmedthat supermarkets using controllers from two other companies were also targeted in the attack.

Toyota Yaris Cross Hybrid 2026 ra mắt Việt Nam, giá tăng nhẹ 5 triệu đồng
Toyota Yaris Cross Hybrid phiên bản nâng cấp 2026 được bổ sung một số chi tiết ngoại thất, gồm ốp cản trước, ốp cản sau và cánh gió thể thao. Giá bán tăng 5 triệu đồng so với trước.
Toyota Yaris Cross Hybrid 2026 tăng giá nhẹ so với bản cũ - Ảnh: Toyota Việt Nam
Ngày 2-11,Toyota Việt Namchính thức giới thiệu Toyota Yaris Cross Hybrid phiên bản nâng cấp 2026, với giá khởi điểm 733 triệu đồng, tăng 5 triệu đồng so với phiên bản trước. Mẫu SUV đô thị này tiếp tục được nhập khẩu nguyên chiếc từ Indonesia.
Những thay đổi trênYaris Cross Hybrid2026 chủ yếu tập trung ở ngoại thất. Phần đầu xe được bổ sung ốp trang trí cản trước với thiết kế mới. Phía sau có thêm ốp cản được thiết kế lại và cánh gió thể thao.
Ba chi tiết này tạo nên sự khác biệt về diện mạo so với phiên bản trước, trong khi thiết kế tổng thể của xe vẫn được giữ nguyên.
Toyota Yaris Cross Hybrid 2026 có 5 lựa chọn màu ngoại thất, gồm trắng ngọc trai, đen, cam nóc đen, xanh nóc đen và trắng ngọc trai nóc đen. Trong đó bản màu trắng ngọc trai có giá 741 triệu đồng, còn màu trắng ngọc trai nóc đen có giá 745 triệu đồng.
Yaris Cross đang là mũi nhọn doanh số của Toyota tại Việt Nam - Ảnh: Toyota Việt Nam
Toyota Yaris Cross Hybrid có kích thước dài, rộng, cao lần lượt 4.310 x 1.770 x 1.655mm, chiều dài cơ sở 2.620mm và khoảng sáng gầm 210mm. Xe được bố trí 5 chỗ ngồi.
Mẫu SUV này tiếp tục sử dụng hệ truyền động hybrid kết hợp động cơ xăng 1.5L, 4 xi lanh, công suất 90 mã lực và mô men xoắn 121Nm với mô tơ điện công suất 79 mã lực, mô men xoắn 141Nm.
Xe sử dụng hộp số tự động vô cấp và hệ dẫn động cầu trước. Theo công bố củaToyota, mức tiêu thụ nhiên liệu kết hợp của Yaris Cross Hybrid là 3,8 lít/100km.
Ngoài những chi tiết ngoại thất mới, xe tiếp tục có hệ thống đèn LED trước và sau, đèn sương mù LED, mâm hợp kim 18 inch, gương chiếu hậu chỉnh điện, gập điện và thanh giá nóc.
Hyundai Palisade hybrid bắt đầu giao xe, khách mua từ tháng sau có thể phải chờĐỌC NGAY
Bên trong, Toyota Yaris Cross Hybrid được trang bị ghế bọc da, ghế lái chỉnh điện 8 hướng, vô lăng 3 chấu tích hợp các phím chức năng và màn hình đa thông tin TFT 7 inch.
Các tiện nghi khác gồm màn hình giải trí cảm ứng 10 inch, kết nối Apple CarPlay và Android Auto, hệ thống âm thanh 6 loa, sạc điện thoại không dây, điều hòa tự động và cửa gió cho hàng ghế sau.
Mẫu xe này còn có phanh tay điện tử, cốp đóng mở điện và trần kính toàn cảnh với tấm che nắng chỉnh điện.
Về an toàn, Toyota Yaris Cross Hybrid 2026 tiếp tục được trang bị gói Toyota Safety Sense, gồm cảnh báo tiền va chạm, cảnh báo lệch làn đường, hỗ trợ giữ làn, điều khiển hành trình chủ động và đèn chiếu xa tự động.
Ngoài ra xe còn có cảnh báo điểm mù, cảnh báo phương tiện cắt ngang phía sau, camera 360 độ, cảm biến hỗ trợ đỗ xe trước và sau cùng 6 túi khí.
Toyota Yaris Cross được giới thiệu tại Việt Nam từ tháng 9-2023. Tính đến hết tháng 10-2026, mẫu xe này đạt doanh số cộng dồn 42.813 chiếc, trong đó phiên bản hybrid đóng góp 4.507 chiếc, tương đương khoảng 11%.
Nhiều người Nhật thích xe Toyota Yaris Cross bán ở Việt Nam hơn xe nội địa
Toyota Yaris Cross mang đến những cảm xúc lẫn lộn cho người dùng. Một hiện tượng khá thú vị là Yaris Cross được bán ở thị trường Đông Nam Á nhận được nhiều đánh giá tích cực từ người tiêu dùng Nhật Bản - nơi được phân phối một phiên bản khác.

Ô tô - Xe máyThứ hai, 02/11/2026 - 11:58
Loạt ô tô mới dự kiến ra mắt Việt Nam tháng 11: Hầu hết là SUV
(Dân trí) - Thị trường ô tô Việt Nam dự kiến đón loạt xe mới trong tháng 11, nổi bật là Mazda CX-5 thế hệ thứ ba, cùng các mẫu xe điện và hybrid như Volvo ES90, EX90, Subaru Forester e-Boxer Hybrid và iCaur V27.
Cuối năm luôn là dịp các hãng xe tận dụng ra mắt sản phẩm mới nhằm đáp ứng nhu cầu mua sắmô tôcủa người Việt. Năm nay không phải ngoại lệ. Sau tháng 10 bùng nổ với 14 mẫu xe điện hóa, thị trường ô tô dự kiến đón nhiều cái tên mới tháng 11, tập trung vào hai xu hướng chính: gầm cao và sử dụng động cơ điện hóa.
Ngày 6/11, Volvo sẽ chính thức ra mắt bộ đôi xe thuần điện mới, bao gồm ES90 và EX90, tại thị trường Việt Nam. Việc giới thiệu hai sản phẩm này nằm trong chiến dịch điện hóa toàn cầu của thương hiệu xe sang Thụy Điển.
Trước đó, trong dải sản phẩm của Volvo Việt Nam đã có sự xuất hiện của mẫu xe thuần điện EC40.
Volvo ES90 (bên trái) và EX90 (bên phải) ra mắt thị trường Việt Nam vào ngày 6/11 (Ảnh: Volvo Việt Nam).
Hai mẫu xe đánh dấu bước chuyển mình quan trọng của Volvo trong kỷ nguyên điện hóa, khi được phát triển trên nền tảng điện áp 800V, cho phép sạc pin từ 10% lên 80% trong vòng 22 phút bằng trạm sạc nhanh DC công suất cao trong điều kiện lý tưởng.
Cả hai mẫu xe này sẽ được nhập khẩu nguyên chiếc từ Malaysia, nhưng trang bị chi tiết chưa được hé lộ. Qua hình ảnh được công bố bởi Volvo Việt Nam, ES90 là mẫu sedan có kiểu dáng fastback, trong khi đó EX90 là dòng SUV cỡ lớn. Có thể xem đây là phiên bản thuần điện của dòng xe động cơ đốt trong S90 và XC90.
Subaru Việt Nam dự kiến tổ chức chương trình ra mắt và trải nghiệm Forester Hybrid dành cho giới truyền thông vào ngày 11/11. Đây sẽ là mẫu xe xăng lai điện thứ 2 của thương hiệu Nhật tại Việt Nam, sau Crosstrek.
Subaru Forester e-Boxer Hybrid ra mắt thị trường Việt ngày 11/11 (Ảnh: MotorTrend).
Tuy nhiên, khác với "đàn em" Crosstrek sử dụng cấu hình mild-hybrid, Subaru Forester Hybrid sẽ được trang bị hệ truyền động thuần hybrid (full-hybrid), gồm máy xăng 2.5L (162 mã lực, 209Nm) kết hợp mô-tơ điện (118 mã lực, 270Nm) và pin lithium-ion dung lượng 1,1kWh.
Hệ truyền động trên tạo ra tổng công suất 194 mã lực, đi kèm hộp số vô cấp eCVT và hệ dẫn động bốn bánh đối xứng toàn thời gian S-AWD. Xe sẽ được nhập khẩu nguyên chiếc từ Nhật Bản giống như các sản phẩm khác của Subaru Việt Nam.
Cùng ngày 11/11, iCaur cũng tổ chứcsự kiệnra mắt thương hiệu tại Việt Nam với mẫu xe đầu tiên V27. iCaur là thương hiệu thuộc tập đoàn Chery (Trung Quốc), ra mắt vào năm 2023, chuyên sản xuất các dòng xe năng lượng mới mang phong cách địa hình việt dã. Tại thị trường nội địa Trung Quốc, thương hiệu này có tên iCar.
V27 là sản phẩm đầu tiên của iCaur tại Việt Nam (Ảnh: Nguyễn Lâm).
iCaur V27 là mẫu xe gầm cao sử dụng hệ thống EREV/REEV (xe điện mở rộng phạm vi). Theo công bố của nhà sản xuất, xe phân phối tại Việt Nam gắn hệ truyền động REEV gồm động cơ xăng kết hợp mô-tơ điện, cho công suất 449 mã lực và mô-men xoắn 505Nm, đi kèm hệ dẫn động bốn bánh bằng điện.
Xe được trang bị bộ pin có dung lượng 34,41kWh, hỗ trợ sạc nhanh từ 20% lên 80% trong vòng 30 phút.
Kích thước iCaur V27 tương đồng với dòng xe địa hình Land Rover Defender 110. Ngoài ra, thiết kế ngoại thất cũng gợi liên tưởng đến mẫu SUV của hãng xe Anh quốc, đặc biệt là cụm đèn chiếu sáng trước/sau và tạo hình thân xe vuông vức.
Sau gần 4 tháng công bố, Volkswagen ID. Era 9X đã xuất hiện tại Việt Nam và được giới tư vấn bán hàng thông báo thời gian giao xe dự kiến bắt đầu từ tháng 11. Theo hãng xe Đức, ID. Era 9X có giá dự kiến dưới 3 tỷ đồng.
Volkswagen ID. Era 9X tiếp nối xu hướng xe điện mở rộng phạm vi tại Việt Nam (Ảnh: Volkswagen).
Volkswagen ID. Era 9X được nhập khẩu nguyên chiếc từ Trung Quốc. Mẫu xe này được phát triển bởi liên doanh SAIC Volkswagen.
Điểm khác biệt của ID. Era 9X là sử dụng hệ truyền động EREV/REEV (xe điện mở rộng phạm vi). Ở cấu hình này, động cơ xăng chỉ làm nhiệm vụ phát điện để sạc pin, không truyền công suất trực tiếp tới bánh xe. Tại Trung Quốc, xe có phạm vi hoạt động thuần điện hơn 400km, theo tiêu chuẩn thử nghiệm CLTC.
Theo Volkswagen Việt Nam, phiên bản bán trong nước sẽ sử dụng hai mô-tơ điện dẫn động bốn bánh với tổng công suất 510 mã lực và mô-men xoắn cực đại 660Nm. Động cơ xăng tăng áp 1.5L công suất 141 mã lực đóng vai trò máy phát điện.
Tháng 12/2025, trong khuôn khổ sự kiện giới thiệu Mazda Flagship (showroom cao cấp) đầu tiên tại Việt Nam và Đông Nam Á, hãng xe Nhật Bản đã trưng bày 4 mẫu xe mới.
Trong đó, Mazda CX-5 thế hệ mới là mẫu xe được chờ đợi nhất, dự kiến ra mắt thị trường vào tháng 11 năm nay. Hiện tại, website Mazda Việt Nam đã cập nhật trang giới thiệu sản phẩm dành riêng cho mẫu xe này, cho thấy ngày ra mắt đã rất gần.
Mazda CX-5 thế hệ mới trưng bày tại đại lý Mazda Flagship (Ảnh: Phùng Thế Anh).
Thế hệ thứ 3 của Mazda CX-5 lần đầu được giới thiệu tại châu Âu vào tháng 7/2025 với kiểu dáng góc cạnh và hầm hố, thay cho những đường nét mềm mại ở đời cũ.Nội thấtcũng có nhiều thay đổi, với điểm nhấn là cụm đồng hồ kỹ thuật số 10,25 inch sau vô lăng và màn hình giải trí 8 inch.
Xe sử dụng động cơ xăng 2.5L hút khí tự nhiên, cho công suất 140 mã lực và mô-men xoắn 238Nm, kết hợp mô-tơ điện mild-hybrid 24V, hộp số tự động 6 cấp và hệ dẫn động cầu trước. Ngoài ra, xe còn có phiên bản thuần xăng, sử dụng động cơ 2.5L.
Tesla chọn ngách nào tại Việt Nam khi VinFast đang dẫn đầu thị trường ô tô?
Thuế nhập khẩu, hạ tầng sạc và vị thế hiện tại của VinFast khiến Tesla nhiều khả năng cạnh tranh ở phân khúc ô tô điện cao cấp.
Phân khúc SUV cỡ lớn tại Việt Nam “nóng” trở lại
Hyundai Palisade Hybrid, Mazda CX-90, Lynk & Co 900 hay Toyota Land Cruiser HEV là những dòng SUV cỡ lớn thu hút được nhiều sự quan tâm của người dùng Việt.
Mitsubishi Pajero thế hệ mới gây sốt ở nhiều thị trường
Lượng đơn đặt hàng và thể hiện sự quan tâm đến mẫu Mitsubishi Pajero thế hệ mới đều rất cao ở cả ba thị trường đầu tiên mà mẫu xe này có mặt, gồm Thái Lan, Australia và Nhật Bản.
Hyundai bàn giao lô xe Palisade Hybrid đầu tiên tới người dùng Việt
Những chiếc Hyundai Palisade Hybrid đầu tiên được bàn giao tới khách hàng tại Việt Nam từ ngày 30/10, không lâu sau khi mẫu xe công bố giá bán.

is a senior science reporter covering energy and the environment with more than a decade of experience. She is also the host ofHell or High Water: When Disaster Hits Home, a podcast from Vox Media and Audible Originals.
A high-stakes California ballot measure pitched as a fast track for “essential” infrastructure could wind up giving data center developers a loophole to evade public scrutiny, environmental advocates warn.
Proposition 45 would shorten timelines for state-mandated environmental assessments for eligible projects and make it more difficult for residents to challenge those projects in court. Proponents say passing the measure would help alleviate the state’shousing shortageand meet rising electricity demand with new renewable energy projects. Environmental groups and some legal experts, however, warn that data center developers backing the proposition could escape scrutiny if Prop 45 becomes law.
“The concern here is that data center developers will find a way to shoehorn their projects into the definition of an essential project and then get to take advantage of … the fast-track review that it’ll create,” says Fernando Gaytan, a senior attorney at the nonprofit environmental law organization Earthjustice, which opposes Prop 45. “Communities get cut out of the conversation.”
“Communities get cut out of the conversation.”
Prop 45 would loosen standards for certain projects subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). CEQA requires state agencies to perform environmental reviews and work with project developers to find ways to limit any harmful impacts to the environment and public health. Crucially, CEQA also mandates that state agencies gather community input and consider public comment before issuing any approvals.
Specifically, Prop 45 would create a365-day deadlinefor agencies to complete the environmental impact report for a project. It also stipulates that any legal challenges would need to be settled within 270 days. It would only allow for 45 days of public comment, and it would only require state agencies and developers to consult with Native American tribes that have been federally recognized. CEQA as it’s currently written sets a minimum rather than a maximum number of days for public review, and mandates consultation with tribes that might be impacted by a project even if they’re not formally recognized by the federal government as having “government-to-government” relations with the US.
During the CEQA review process, state agencies develop alternatives that developers can take to mitigate environmental and health risks. Prop 45 would turn that on its head, making developers responsible for coming up with a single alternative project plan for regulators to consider. The proposition would also strip away an agency’s authority to repeatedly ask a developer for more information about a proposed project; state regulators would need to specify all the information a company is required to provide at the start of the application process.
On top of all that, Prop 45 would bar courts from halting a project altogether even if it finds that the regulatory agency failed to correctly comply with CEQA. The judge would only have the ability to pause specific parts of a project that are problematic, rather than forcing a full stop to construction. That’s the piece that’s most egregious for Gaytan. “It’s hard to undo harms once you’ve already started a project,” he says.
Data centers are ahot-buttonelectionissuefor midterms across the US and have become a point of contention for Prop 45 as well. The proposition lists nine types of “essential” projects that would be eligible for streamlined review, including housing, clean energy, and “broadband Internet access.”
Gaytan and someother legal experts contendthat the latter designation — broadband internet access — could include data centers. Thelanguageincludes any project that would “provide mass-market retail service by wire service, wireless service, or radio to customers in this state that provides the capability to transmit data to, and receive data from, all or substantially all internet endpoints, including, but not limited to, any capabilities that are incidental to and enable the operation of the communications service.”
Data center backlash is uniting America
Proposed data centers that include any broadband transmission infrastructure might be able to squeeze into that definition, UC Davis School of Law professor emeritus Richard Frank and attorney Matthew McKerley write in a recentcolumnin theDaily Journal.They also point out that companies currently developing data centers have poured hundreds of thousands of dollars into a campaign to support Prop 45. And while Prop 45 excludes certain types of projects, like nuclear energy and dial-up internet access service, it doesn’t explicitly bar data centers.
Proponents, meanwhile, argue that Prop 45 would not apply to data centers. “The fact that data centers may play a role in supporting the Internet does not make them ‘essential broadband Internet access projects’ under Prop 45,” attorney and lobbyist Kurt OnetowritesinThe National Law Review. The Yes on Prop 45 campaign didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Guardian Essential poll: record number of Australians are turning their backs on the Melbourne Cup | Melbourne Cup | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
More than two-thirds of Australian polled now say they have low or zero interest in the annual Melbourne Cup horse race.Photograph: Robert Cianflone/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMore than two-thirds of Australian polled now say they have low or zero interest in the annual Melbourne Cup horse race.Photograph: Robert Cianflone/Getty Images
Guardian Essential poll: record number of Australians are turning their backs on the Melbourne Cup
Growing disdain for gambling and animal cruelty concerns drive sliding interest in race that once ‘stopped the nation’
Get ourbreaking news email,free appordaily news podcast
A record number of Australians are turning their backs on theMelbourne Cup, with more than two-thirds surveyed saying they have low or zero interest in the annual horse race.
Support for the Melbourne Cup has been sliding consistently for a number of years, butthe Guardian Essential pollfound just 9% of Australians said they had high interest in the race now – nearly half the proportion in 2025.
“The race that once stopped the nation is now just white noise for many,” Peter Lewis, chair of Essential Media, said.
The Guardian Essential poll of 1,003 Australians in late October highlights thelatest erosionin popularity of the eventamid growing ambivalence to the event.
Guardian Essential poll: One Nation and Labor’s primary vote on par as discontent with Albanese risesRead more
Just 9% of people said they had high interest in the Cup, down 7 percentage points from 2025, with another 23% professing moderate interest, also down 3 points. About 29% of voters said they had low interest (up 5 points from last year), while another 39% said no interest at all (up 8 points).
The combined high and moderate interest came to only 32%, the lowest on record since Essential began asking this question in annual polling in November 2022. The combined low and no interest vote was 68%, jumping 12 points from last year to its highest on record.
Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email
In November 2022, the low and no interest vote came to a combined 52%; it was 62% in 2023, 52% in 2024, and 56% in 2025.
The“nup to the Cup” movement, backed by some high-profile politicians and celebrities, has contributed to declining support for the race.
But 62% of Australians nonetheless agreed the Melbourne Cup was a unique part of Australia’s national identity. That number remains a strong majority view, despite falling from 78% agreement when Essential asked this question in 2019.
Half of Australians (50%) believe the Cup promotes unhealthy gambling behaviour, up 3% since 2025, while 36% say they feel the Cup normalises animal cruelty, down 3 points from 2025.
Another 48% said they were less interested in the Cup than they used to be.
“The key driver appears to be a growing disdain for gambling, although concern for animal cruelty comes a close second,” Lewis said.
“More broadly this reflects the decline in unifying atonal moments in a world where more and more people have their experiences mediated by targeted advertising algorithms.”
Just 12% of voters in October’s poll said they regularly wagered on horse races and would bet on Tuesday’s Melbourne Cup, down 5 points from 2025. In contrast, 46% of people said they were not interested in the Cup and would not place a bet, up 6 points from last year.
Another 25% said they rarely bet on horses but would watch the race and place a bet, while 17% said they would watch but not bet.

Race walker Isaac Beacroft (left) is one of many Australian Olympic medal hopes, so long as his sport is included in the final program.Photograph: Jane Barlow/PAView image in fullscreenRace walker Isaac Beacroft (left) is one of many Australian Olympic medal hopes, so long as his sport is included in the final program.Photograph: Jane Barlow/PA
Brisbane 2032: the sports being forced to modernise in bid to stay in Olympic race
Microchips, ninja obstacle courses and other ‘modern’ tweaks are being made by sports vying for a coveted spot on the Olympic program in Australia
Australia’s teenage race walker Isaac Beacroft won gold at the Commonwealth Games this year, propelling him into contention for a medal at the home Brisbane Olympics in six years’ time. There is just one problem.
The International Olympic Committee is considering culling events like his – as well as surfing, skateboarding and climbing, in which Australia also has strong podium chances – in secretive deliberations under way in Switzerland that are set to transform the Olympic program.
Warning over future of Olympic Games if Brisbane 2032 program is not modernisedRead more
Officials within sports are not watching idly while their fates are determined in Lausanne, however. Modern pentathlon has ditched its horse riding component for a ninja obstacle course. Canoe sprint is moving away from longer distances to focus on the more dramatic, explosive 500m events.
Some in race walking, like Beacroft, have their own plan: a microchip in competitors’ shoes. The 19-year-old, who won gold in Glasgow thanks toa final-lap surge, says the chip – alongside shifting the event distance from 20,000 metres to the more broadly relatable half marathon – is “the race walkers’ play to keep it in the Olympics”.
The chip “detects the flight time” of walkers, Beacroft explains, thereby eliminating the subjectivity from judging. “That’s going to go a long way in creating some sort of reliability and respect towards the sport.”
The tiny contraption could be the difference between an Olympic future and a slide away from the sporting spotlight. A planned reduction in the number of sports for Brisbane, a decreased cap of 10,500 athletes, and aneed for the Olympics to moderniseleaves emerging sports competing with traditional pursuits such as fencing and wrestling. The IOC is also assessing each “discipline” – seeing, for example, track and road cycling as separate – based on its television audience, cost and complexity of facilities, and size of athlete cohort.
Chart to show the number of athletes at recent Olympic Games.
The traditional heavyweights are swimming, gymnastics and athletics, the latter with 1,810 competitors at LA 2028 or close to one-fifth of the entire athlete body. Each will retain their place, though some events or disciplines such as race walking may be vulnerable. Meanwhile, sports with bespoke venues like triathlon, or large athlete quotas like rowing and hockey, will be looked at closely in a process dubbed as “fit for future” by the IOC.
As IOC officials enter their final months of decision-making, several of Australia’s potential podium contenders for 2032 including Beacroft, skateboarders Arisa Trew and Chloe Covell, climber Oceana Mackenzie (currently ranked second in the world in bouldering) and surfers like world No 1 Molly Picklum are in jeopardy of missing out if the IOC leaves their disciplines out of the core program.
View image in fullscreenArisa Trew won skateboard gold for Australia at the Paris Olympics.Photograph: Frank Franklin II/AP
Their participation would then require the Brisbane organising committee to include these sports as one of the hosts’ additional picks, limited to four, akin to how breaking was included in Paris. Competition for those places is set to be fierce as Australian favourites like netball, surf lifesaving and touch football join the frenzy of aspirants vying for an Olympic berth.
Chart to show individual sports’ revenue from the IOC for Tokyo 2020
There is another consideration, however, that has officials sweating. The cost of holding the additional sports must be borne by the local organising committee alone, rather than co-funded by the IOC. Organisers therefore face budget overruns if the IOC shunts preferred sports with large numbers of athletes or complex venues from the core program.
This dynamic partly explains the stance by the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, expressed at the Future Brisbane conference last weekend, that Brisbane 2032 officials and the Queensland government should consider using existing facilities in Sydney and Melbourne for sports beyond football, which already has interstate pool games planned.
“One of the things I’ve said is that it’s Queensland’s games, it’s their decision,” he said. “They could consider, just as the Paris Games had surfing in Tahiti, and all of the Games aren’t always just in the city where they’re held, if you want to save money and save time, then you could give consideration to that.”
View image in fullscreenSydney Olympic Park could host some bonus Brisbane 2032 events if the final program requires more facilities.Photograph: David Gray/Getty Images
Co-funded by the state and federal governments, $7.1bn has been committed to Games venue infrastructure, but a detailed budget will not be possible until the IOC decides the final program. That had been expected in 2026, but now all that will be known by the new year is the list of core disciplines, as well some fringe proposals no longer in the running.
Instead, a final decision on the program will not arrive until the IOC session in April next year – a farcical situation around which the Brisbane 2032 president, Andrew Liveris, has already expressed frustration. “I think we’re all very anxious to get that finalised, and for good reasons,” he said at the launch ofthe Games logotwo weeks ago.
Beacroft is confident race walking will make the cut, but says it is not easy for athletes currently in limbo. “You don’t want to be in denial about it or anything like that … I kind of keep my fingers crossed that it’s going to be in Brisbane, because that’s a massive goal of mine and a big, big motivator for my career.”

Hyrox partners with World Triathlon in bid to become Olympic sport - BBC Sport
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Hyrox holds more than 100 events worldwide each year
Hyrox has moved closer to fulfilling its ambition of gaining inclusion into the Olympic and Paralympic Games after entering into a partnership with World Triathlon.
The agreement will see 'hybrid racing' become a recognised discipline within World Triathlon, the sport's global governing body.
Hyrox, the fitness craze which combines running with exercise stations, will be contested across three formats - ultimate, fast and ultra - each sanctioned and governed by World Triathlon.
World Triathlon and Hyrox said in a statement that obtaining Olympic and Paralympic status for the discipline was the "ultimate ambition".
World Triathlon president Antonio Arimany said hybrid racing was "a natural evolution for our movement".
He added: "This partnership will not only accelerate the growth of World Triathlon on the global stage, it will open genuine new opportunities for every one of our national federations to grow participation, engage new audiences, and strengthen our sport at every level.
"This is exactly the kind of forward-looking collaboration our members deserve."
Hyrox co-founder Christian Toetzke said: "From the very beginning, our goal was to build a global sport that could earn a place on the world's biggest athletic stage.
"Partnering with World Triathlon is a monumental step toward that vision.
"Hybrid racing is no longer just a global fitness movement, it is officially on the road to the Olympics."
Great Britain's Olympic triathlon champion Alex Yee reacted to the news by sharing a poll with his 227,000 followers, who had voted 82% against being in favour of the move after a couple of hours.
Fellow British triathlete Max Stapley commented on the joint announcement on Instagram: "This is crap."
Olympic triathlete Roksana Slupek, of Poland, wrote "the two sports have absolutely nothing in common" and questioned what her sport would gain from the partnership.
How Hyrox became the latest sporting craze
Hyrox apologises for allowing race to continue after athlete soils herself
Hyrox was founded in 2017, primarily as an indoor discipline in which athletes take part in eight legs consisting of a one-kilometre run followed by a fitness exercise.
The exercises include 1km on a standing ski machine, 50m sled push, 50m sled pull, 80m burpee jumps, 1km row, 200m kettlebell carry, 100m lunges carrying a sandbag, and 100 throws and catches of a medicine ball against a wall.
World championships are held each year, with athletes contesting both singles and doubles races.
Under the agreement with World Triathlon, Hyrox will continue to oversee world, continental and national championships for elite athletes in the 'ultimate' format, which mirrors its existing format.
The additional formats included under the new discipline of hybrid racing - 'fast' and 'ultra' - offer high intensity and extended adaptations.
Only sports governed by recognised international federations which comply with the Olympic Charter, the World Anti-Doping Code and the Olympic Movement Code on the Prevention of the Manipulation of Competition - as is the case for triathlon - are eligible for inclusion at the Olympic and Paralympic Games.

Millions of Americans are about to decide the future of the Republican-controlled Congress in a midterm election that will have a significant impact on President Donald Trump's final two years in office.

There are seven Senate races deemed to be a toss-up byindependent elections analyst Cook Political Report,external.

This race has been marred by controversy over the appearance of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot. The Republican senator of that name faces stiff competition from Mary Peltola and accuses her of introducing his namesake to confuse voters, which she denies.
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Dan Sullivan is aiming for his third term against Alaska Native Mary Peltola
The race may ultimately be the tipping point state that decides which party controls the chamber if, as expected, Alaska is one of the slower states to reach an outcome.
Peltola, a former House member and the first Alaska Native to be elected to Congress, has run on a platform of "fish, family, freedom" and has attacked Sullivan's record as Alaska's natural resources commissioner.
Two-term senator Sullivan, a long-time Marine Corps reservist who also served as Alaska's attorney general, has accused Peltola's campaign of links to an effort to confuse Republican voters which led to a second man named Dan Sullivan entering the race.
The Peltola campaign denies any such link, though the issue is the subject of a state investigation and a justice department lawsuit, which on Sunday was rejected by a judge.
Alaska's ranked-choice system also adds uncertainty to the mix, and the state has historically been difficult to poll, with surveys historically underestimating Republican voters.
Sullivan, 61, only retired from the US Marines as recently as 2024, after a 30-year career that included deployments in to Afghanistan and the Middle East. Peltola, 53, grew up fishing salmon with her father, later becoming the first person born in the state to actually represent it in Congress.
One of the few Republicans who voted to convict Trump when he was impeached in 2021, longtime senator Susan Collins has outperformed her party in this Democratic-leaning state, partly by presenting herself as a rebel. Her opponent Troy Jackson, who draws on his background as a lumberjack to persuade blue-collar Mainers he can relate to them, hopes that time is finally running out for one of the great survivors of US politics.
Susan Collins, the incumbent, takes on logger Troy Jackson in Maine
Collins is hoping her reputation as a centrist will persuade independent-minded voters in a state that reliably votes Democratic in presidential elections.
Now her campaign will test whether Republicans can win by distancing themselves from Trump.
Collins, who is seeking her sixth term, entered the midterm cycle as one of the most vulnerable incumbent Republicans seeking re-election.
But she has been helped by controversy on the other side of the aisle involving Graham Platner, who was ultimately replaced as the Democratic nominee by Jackson, a former president of the Maine state senate.
Both Jackson and Collins oppose Trump's tariffs on Canada, mindful of the impact they are having on this border state. Unlike Collins, though, he favours the abolition of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency (ICE).
Collins, 73, began her political career fresh from college in the 1970s and she entered the US Senate in 1997. Jackson, 58, is a logger who became politically active when he helped to lead a protest to block lower-paid workers from Canada entering Maine.
James Talarico aims to end a decades-long electoral drought for the Democrats in Texas - and show that one of the Republicans' main strongholds could be in play for the 2028 presidential election. His match-up with Ken Paxton has become the most expensive Senate race ever.
Trump ally Ken Paxton (L) faces a challenge from former teacher James Talarico (R) in the Texas contest
Republican Paxton knows his party has been winning statewide races in Texas for more than 30 years.
Texas State Representative James Talarico, a former schoolteacher and Presbyterian seminary student, is the latest Democrat hoping to break his party's long losing streak.
Texas Republicans are facing a daunting combination of headwinds. It is a challenging national political environment for conservatives and there are several state issues like data centre construction and aggressive immigration enforcement that have cut against their party. Added to that is a controversial candidate, Paxton.
The campaign has been acrimonious, with Talarico targeting Paxton's 2023 impeachment by the Republican-controlled state House of Representatives for alleged corruption, bribery and abuse of power. Paxton denied the charges and was later acquitted by the state Senate, calling the impeachment a "politically motivated sham from the beginning".
Supported by more than $170m in funds from tech mogul Elon Musk, Paxton has attempted to paint Talarico as a liberal who is out of touch with Texans on issues like transgender rights, law enforcement, immigration and energy policy.
A Democratic victory here might indicate America's second-biggest electoral prize in a presidential election could be within their reach in 2028 - a notion that could dramatically reshape the nation's political landscape.
Before he entered public service, Paxton spent 14 years launching and building his own law firm. He served in the state House and Senate before becoming the chief legal officer in Texas.
Talarico taught at a middle school in San Antonio, in a neighbourhood he has described as one of the poorest in the state. He has studied theology and names Pope Leo as a "spiritual hero".

Australia Test captain Pat Cummins to miss upcoming England matches
Starc and Hazlewood also rested before busy summer
Beardman and Shaw set to make their team debuts
Test captain Pat Cummins and fellow quicks Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood will be rested during Australia’s upcoming one-day and T20 series against England.
Australia will play three ODIs and five T20 internationals, but Cummins, Starc and Hazlewood were not named in either squad on Monday as the pace trio refresh for a gruelling 10 Tests in 14 weeks this summer.
Australia’s bizarre selection choices backfired – predictably – in South Africa. It’s time for a reality check | Geoff LemonRead more
Key batsmen Travis Head, Matthew Renshaw, Josh Inglis, Cooper Connolly and all-rounder Cameron Green will be managed through the T20 series following long tours to Zimbabwe and South Africa, as they prepare for four Tests against New Zealand and five in India.
“We are in the middle of a highly demanding phase of our schedule,” said chair of selectors, George Bailey. “Our multi-format players are transitioning directly from the tour of South Africa into an ODI and T20 series, leaving a narrow window to ensure the squad is physically prepared and fresh for the upcoming New Zealand Test series.
“Then, from when the Test players assemble in Perth through to the conclusion of the 150th anniversary Test against England, the team will have been on the road for more than 100 days. To manage this workload, each player’s build-up to the New Zealand series will be carefully planned and focused on individual’s physical and mental preparation.”
Rising WA paceman Mahli Beardman will make his national one-day debut after playing one T20 for Australia.
View image in fullscreenWestern Australian Mahli Beardman (right) has impressed Australia’s selectors.Photograph: James Worsfold/Getty Images
“Mahli Beardman’s recent performances for Australia A were impressive and we are incredibly excited for his return to the national team across the ODI and T20 formats,” Bailey said. “We think he can continue to develop into an all-format player across the coming years.”
Jack Edwards was rewarded for an impressive recent tour of South Africa and consistent domestic cricket performance with a place in both squads. Left-arm quick Spencer Johnson and all-rounder Liam Scott return to the ODI squad. Nathan Ellis has not recovered in time for the ODI series as he returns from a side strain.
The Hobart Hurricanes’ recently crowned Australian T20 player of the year Tim David will spearhead the Twenty20 squad. Hard-hitting opening batter Jake Fraser-McGurk has also won back a place in Australia’s T20 team for the first time since 2025. And promising young NSW batter Lachlan Shaw joins the T20 squad for the first time, having impressed on the recent Australia A tour to India and in the BBL.
The ODI side continues to build towards Australia’s 2027 World Cup defence in Africa, while the T20 squad has a longer-term goal of the 2028 LA Olympics and T20 World Cup.

NFL power rankings: Broncos, Steelers climb after big wins; Vikings, Cowboys and Eagles drop for Week 9
The time between the end of Week 8 and the start of Week 9 marks the new midseason point of the NFL schedule. Although some of the league's better playoff powers are pulling away near the top, there are still a lot of "tightly contested races", apt for mid-term election time, too.
Don't forget that last week was Halloween, setting up some wild results over the weekend. Some teams have clear identities, while some teams are struggling with injuries, inconsistency and inefficiency.
Here's the latest look at how all 32 teams stack up against each other, with no more undefeated teams and still the one winless team:
NFL TRADE DEADLINE RUMORS:12 deals that make sense
1. Buffalo Bills 6-1 (previous ranking: 1)
Josh Allen, for the 54th time in his nine-year career, delivered both a passing and rushing TD in the same game in beating theRavens. He also has a total of 259 passing TDs combined in the regular season and playoffs, breaking Jim Kelly's long-time franchise record. The only thing missing from Allen's resume is the Super Bowl. He is on his way to his second MVP to lock up his Hall of Fame spot.
The49ersare coming off a bye to recover from their only loss of the season and Brock Purdy's worst game of the season against theFalcons. Purdy has also been sacked seven times in the past three games after taking none in the first four. He has a pair of get-well games coming up, however, against theRaiders' andCowboys' defenses.
Bo Nix can keep laughing at critics after recording his fourth fourth-quarter comeback and fifth game-winning drive of the season against theChiefs. He led the league with seven game-winning drives last season. Nix's numbers still aren't pretty, but he has a knack for clutch plays that get the job done.
Go figure: Kyler Murray threw more than one TD pass in a game for the first time this season in Detroit but that added up to the first loss of the season. He's still not pushing the ball downfield well enough for Kevin O'Connell. Minnesota can no longer get away with an anemic offense and keep putting undue pressure on the stellar defense.
Patrick Mahomes got back on track with his passing in Denver, timed with the return of Rashee Rice as his top wide receiver. Andy Reid can point to one big reason why the Chiefs lost to theBroncos. They had a season-high 11 penalties go against them, after having only 41 in the previous six games, the second-lowest total in the NFL.
MORE:Andy Reid disagrees with game-changing offsides call
Caleb Williams vs. theSeahawks' defense will be a fun battle to watch on Monday night. Will his improv neutralize the pass rush and wear down the coverage? Or will Williams revert to some old turnover woes? Should Williams pass the test in hostile Seattle, there might emerge a new team to beat in the NFC.
TheJaguarsimproved to 11-4 in the regular season when Trevor Lawrence has three or more passing TDs in routing theColtson Sunday. What Bhayshul Tuten is doing as a second-year feature back has been huge for Liam Coen's offense.
Mike Tomlin would be proud of this Steelers' edition. They ran for 200 yards against the Browns on only 33 attempts. They are averaging 4.9 yards per carry this season, up to No. 3 in the NFL behind only the Chiefs and Buccaneers. They are also No. 3 in run defense, allowing an average of 83.9 yards per game.
MORE:Why Steelers are positioned to run away in AFC North race
The Seahawks prepared well for facing Williams, flustering Mahomes into a career-low game in prime time in Week 7. Seattle's pass defense is nasty this season, allowing an average of 144.4 yards per game and only eight touchdowns in seven games.
The Patriots had neither A.J. Brown nor TreVeyon Henderson to raise the big-play quotient in the offense, but Drake Maye still passed for 8.7 yards per attempt, and the team still rushed for 131 yards to beat the Dolphins. They won't give the Bills much breathing room in the AFC East.
The Lions have come through with huge back-to-back home division wins against the Packers and Vikings. The big surprise is the improved defense. After allowing an average of almost 30 points in the first five games, the Lions have given up only 32 total the past two weeks. They should keep up that play with the Dolphins in Miami next.
Joe Burrow is on pace for 49 TD passes and 5,136 yards and raised his league-best completion percentage to 73.0. It's a roller-coaster ride with his turnovers at times but as long as he's healthy, the Bengals are a real threat to win Super Bowl 60.
MORE:How Burrow passing his way into NFL MVP consideration
The Rams have become a more effective, more committed running team with new downfield passing constraints for Matthew Stafford and the offense minus Davante Adams. Sean McVay's heavy reliance on Kyren Williams and Blake Corum for chunk rushing has delivered out of necessity.
The Packers faced the atrocious Panthers' run defense in Week 8, but they still are last in the NFL in rushing offense, averaging a microscopic 60 yards per game. Matt LaFleur is smart to keep running to provide balance even with limited results, because it still supports the league's No. 2 passing offense.
The Giants come out of the bye with the No. 15 rushing offense in the NFL. They will hope to keep that number climbing with Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary with Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) on injured reserve. That's been key to unlocking J.J. McCarthy, who averaged 10.1 yards per pass attempt in his Week 7 start at Houston.
The Browns are starting to spring more leaks in their run defense, but the bigger problem up front is their offensive line, which gave up eight sacks on Deshaun Watson and helped to produce only 34 rushing yards in Pittsburgh. Watson is on pace to be sacked an NFL-high 70 times, which would challenge the record set by fellow former Texan David Carr.
The Ravens' passing game went kaput against the Bills' bad pass defense after both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley went down with injuries. At the same time, the Ravens' defense gave up 417 total yards and was on the field for more than 37 minutes. Even more worrisome is the fact Derrick Henry has been contained to only 156 combined rushing yards in the past three games.

Cfoto | Future Publishing | Getty Images
Binance said it recorded $3.64 billion in net outflows after reopening withdrawals on Sunday following a $6.3 billion hack, as customers rushed to move funds off the platform.
The exchange processed $4.65 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits between 6 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. UTC on Nov. 1, Binancesaidin a post on X.
The resulting net outflows represented 2.1% of Binance's $171 billion in total assets, based on its latest available proof-of-reserves data as of Oct. 28.
Binance said withdrawal volumes had declined and were stabilizing following an initial spike, while deposit volumes remained substantial.
The exchange began restoring withdrawals in phases at 6 a.m. UTC on Sunday, with services resuming across all 15 networks and assets included in the initial phase by 12:36 p.m. UTC. It said testing was continuing for the remaining networks and assets.
"Circle activated its incident response procedures and coordinated with law enforcement to freeze more than $1.1 billion in USDC associated with the incident," a spokesperson for the stablecoin issuer told CNBC in an email. The company said the investigation is ongoing.
The updated figure follows a Fridaypostfrom Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire, who said at the time that more than $800 million in USDC linked to the incident had been frozen.
Binance founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao sought to reassure users following the breach,writingon X that "98% choose to stay!" He said most of the net outflows occurred within the first couple of hours after withdrawals resumed. "Trust isn't earned by what you say in good times. It's earned by what you do in hard times," Zhao added.
The withdrawals followed a record $6.3 billion hack of Binance last week. The FBIattributedthe attack to North Korean hackers, identifying the operation as TraderTraitor.
The exchange has said it wouldabsorbthe financial impact of the stolen funds rather than pass the losses on to users.
Binance said it had coveredaround 95%of the impacted amount, up from 90% in its previous update. The exchange said the remaining 5% consisted of less liquid tokens that would take longer to source in the quantities required.
